newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM aluminium ends up in buoyant trade on dollar.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM aluminium ends up in buoyant trade on dollar.

text.p: Tokyo yen-based aluminium futures finished higher in buoyant trade on Monday due to the dollar's rise against the yen and higher prices on the London Metal Exchange (LME), traders said.
"Aluminium's fairly strong on the LME. A perception that the dollar will stay strong also buoyed market sentiment," said one trader.
The June contract was up 3.2 yen at 202.0 yen per kg and the April added 3.6 yen to end at 204.0. The spot October rose by its daily limit of 6.0 yen to close at 207.1.
In London on Friday, where zinc climbed higher on waves of speculative buying, three month aluminium rose $31 to a peak of $1,691, the highest since March 7.
Traders said the next target was the $1,701 high marked on March 4 this year.
